title: ec2bedrock-cli ships its first milestone: the ec2bedrock CLI can define inference profiles and answer 'is self-managed EC2 cheaper than a token provider for this ADLC workload?' — estimate scheduled EC2 cost, compare against token-provider pricing, and explain break-even utilization — entirely offline, dry-run by default, with JSON output for a future ADLC router, and zero AWS mutation.

targets.text: ec2bedrock-cli ships its first milestone: the ec2bedrock CLI can define inference profiles and answer 'is self-managed EC2 cheaper than a token provider for this ADLC workload?' — estimate scheduled EC2 cost, compare against token-provider pricing, and explain break-even utilization — entirely offline, dry-run by default, with JSON output for a future ADLC router, and zero AWS mutation.
estimate, compare, and break-even all run with no network and no boto3 installed; --json emits a documented stable schema; no command mutates AWS.
ADLC/Culture engineers and the future model router deciding whether to wake EC2 GPU capacity or call a token provider, plus AWS clients evaluating self-hosted inference economics.
the JSON output is router-consumable: stable keys + an explicit decision field + an exit code that encodes the recommendation, not just human-readable text.

An engineer runs 'ec2bedrock profile show qwen27b-awq-l40s', 'ec2bedrock estimate --profile … --hours 8 --days 22', and 'ec2bedrock compare --profile … --input-tokens … --output-tokens …' and gets a costed EC2-vs-token-provider recommendation with break-even utilization — no AWS account, nothing launched.
all three commands produce correct, reproducible numbers from profile+args alone with zero AWS credentials present.
Today ec2bedrock-cli is the culture-agent-template introspection scaffold (whoami/learn/explain/overview/doctor, empty runtime deps); issue #1's plan exists only as prose, no cost or profile logic.

the new cost/profile code is additive — the existing introspection scaffold (whoami/learn/explain/overview/doctor) and its tests pass unchanged; the ONLY new runtime dep is ec2-cli (itself boto3-free on a base install); config parsing is stdlib tomllib.
ADLC only pays off when sustained office-hours agent work beats token-provider economics; you must prove the economics on paper before spending on GPUs or building lifecycle/serving machinery.
compare output states a clear recommendation (EC2 / token-provider / mixed) AND the break-even utilization, so economics are legible, not just two totals.

Issue #1's six first-milestone acceptance criteria pass: define a profile, estimate scheduled EC2 cost, compare against token-provider cost, explain break-even utilization, emit router JSON, and run dry-run with no AWS mutation — verified by tests with zero network/boto3.
each of the six acceptance criteria maps to at least one passing test; the suite runs fully offline in CI.
Every command supports --json with a documented stable schema; estimate and compare also encode the recommendation in the process exit code so a router can branch on it.
estimate --json and compare --json validate against a documented schema in tests; compare's exit code maps deterministically to {EC2 / token-provider / mixed} and is documented.
The break-even output answers issue #1's question: output-only break-even tokens/sec AND an input+output-aware break-even, so context-heavy ADLC workloads are modelled, not just output.

break-even is reported two ways — output-only tokens/sec, and an input+output-aware figure given an assumed input:output ratio — matching issue #1's worked numbers (≈172 tok/s output-only; EC2 wins earlier once input is included).

Milestone 1 does NOT launch/stop/hibernate EC2 (Stage 2), does NOT serve a model/run vLLM (Stage 3), does NOT do schedules/fallback/Blackwell (Stages 5/6/8), and does NOT touch a live AWS account or the Pricing API — pricing is computed offline from the profile's hourly_usd plus ec2-cli's boto3-free estimate_cost arithmetic, never a live rate lookup.

no milestone-1 code path imports boto3 or opens a socket; a test asserts estimate/compare/decide do not import boto3 and that pricing is read only from the profile + ec2-cli's boto3-free pricing module (no live AWS / Pricing API).

tasks.summary: ec2-cli coupling adapter + dependency pin + offline/no-boto3 guard
acceptance_criteria: pyproject adds ec2-cli as the only new runtime dependency, pinned to a version whose ec2.aws.pricing API is verified at import

ec2bedrock/cost/_ec2cli.py re-exports estimate_cost + Estimate; a test asserts estimate_cost accepts kwargs ondemand_rate/spot_rate/running_hours/ebs_monthly and that importing it does NOT pull boto3 into sys.modules
a static test asserts no module under ec2bedrock/cost imports boto3 at top level and no milestone-1 path opens a socket

ec2bedrock/cost/profiles.py defines a Profile dataclass (instance_type, gpu, runtime, quantization, hourly_usd, storage_gb, performance, lifecycle, budgets) and a DEFAULT_PROFILES registry with qwen27b-awq-l40s as a Python literal (g6e.xlarge/l40s-48gb/vllm/awq/1.861/200)
Profile round-trips to a plain dict for --json; unknown config fields raise a clear CliError, not a traceback

tasks.summary: config.toml loader over bundled defaults (stdlib tomllib)
acceptance_criteria: ec2bedrock/cost/config.py loads ~/.ec2bedrock/config.toml via stdlib tomllib, returning resolved profiles + token-provider pricing + budgets; missing file falls back to bundled defaults with no error
a user profile of the same name in config.toml overrides the bundled default; a test proves override + extend semantics

tasks.summary: Bundled rate data (EBS GB-month + default provider prices)
acceptance_criteria: ec2bedrock/cost/rates.py exposes an EBS USD/GB-month rate (cited from ec2-cli rates concept) and default token-provider prices (input 0.58, output 3.01 USD/1M), each overridable; lookups return None/default and never raise

ec2bedrock/cost/estimate.py estimate(profile, hours, days) returns an estimate where compute = hourly_usd*hours*days and ebs derives from storage_gb*ebs_rate, computed via ec2.aws.pricing.estimate_cost with the rate injected from the profile
estimate degrades to an UNKNOWN total (no crash) when a rate is missing, mirroring ec2-cli Estimate semantics; numbers reproduce with zero AWS credentials present
ec2bedrock/cost/breakeven.py computes output-only break-even tokens/sec from hourly_usd and provider output price, matching issue #1's ~172 tok/s worked figure
computes an input+output-aware break-even given an assumed input:output ratio, demonstrating EC2 wins earlier once input is included (issue #1 worked example)

tasks.summary: compare: EC2 vs token-provider -> recommendation + exit code
acceptance_criteria: ec2bedrock/cost/compare.py compare(...) returns ec2_usd, provider_usd, a recommendation in {ec2, token-provider, mixed}, and the break-even; provider cost = input*in_price + output*out_price
the recommendation maps to a documented, deterministic process exit code; a test asserts the mapping and the unknown-degradation path

tasks.summary: decide --json: workload-class + sensitive -> verdict + exit code
acceptance_criteria: ec2bedrock/cost/decide.py decide(workload, input_tokens, output_tokens, sensitive) returns {decision, reason, exit}; sensitive=true -> ec2, sporadic/off-hours -> token-provider, else cost-driven via compare
output is router-consumable: stable JSON keys + explicit decision field + exit code encoding the recommendation

ec2bedrock/cli/_commands/profile.py exposes register(sub) adding 'profile list' and 'profile show <name>' with --json; a test builds a throwaway parser, registers, and asserts list+show output for the bundled default WITHOUT touching cli/__init__.py

tasks.summary: estimate/compare/decide CLI commands (thin wrappers, file-disjoint per verb)
acceptance_criteria: ec2bedrock/cli/_commands/{estimate,compare,decide}.py each expose register(sub): estimate --profile --hours --days; compare --profile --input-tokens --output-tokens --provider-input-price --provider-output-price; decide --workload --input-tokens --output-tokens --sensitive; all support --json
each command's --json validates against the documented schema and the process exit code matches the domain recommendation; tested per-command via a throwaway parser, not the global parser

tasks.summary: Wire verbs into the CLI + end-to-end integration test
acceptance_criteria: cli/__init__.py registers profile/estimate/compare/decide alongside the existing introspection verbs; the existing scaffold verbs and their tests pass unchanged
an integration test drives main(['profile','show','qwen27b-awq-l40s']), main(['estimate',...]), main(['compare',...]), main(['decide',...,'--json']) end-to-end offline and asserts exit codes

tasks.summary: explain catalog + README quickstart for the new verbs
acceptance_criteria: ec2bedrock/explain/catalog.py gains entries for profile/estimate/compare/decide; README documents the milestone-1 quickstart matching the spec's after-state commands
teken rubric still passes (explain ec2bedrock resolves) and markdownlint is clean

tasks.summary: Acceptance-criteria matrix test (six M1 criteria, offline)
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_acceptance_m1.py asserts each of issue #1's six first-milestone criteria (define profile, estimate, compare, break-even, router JSON, dry-run/no-mutation) maps to >=1 passing assertion
the whole suite runs with no network and no boto3 installed; a guard asserts boto3 absence on the milestone-1 paths
pyproject + ec2bedrock/__init__.py bumped to 0.4.0; CHANGELOG gets a Keep-a-Changelog entry; version-check CI passes (0.4.0 > main 0.3.2)

risks.text: ec2-cli 0.6.0 (issue #4: final injected-rate estimate_cost signature + rates table) is unreleased; PyPI tops at 0.5.0. T1 must pin to a version whose pricing API it verifies against, or sequence M1 behind ec2-cli's 0.6.0 release.
